messages.author: d560d9e01924933c
messages.subject: INLA posterior sample
parts:
Hi,

It is just amazing getting samples from a fitted model using
inla.posterior.sample, because we can use Monte Carlo like approach
and estimate the posterior distribution of all sort of non linear
combinations of one or more parameters. This is very powerful.

Having said that, I would like to know if there is any reference for
the accuracy of the samples of the approximate posterior distribution
using inla.posterior.samples. Or shall I need to somehow validate my
samples for every new model I use?

It would be great if there is a paper on this, I would love to learn
how the hyperparameters are sampled. Since they are also important to
sample the latent field, as I understood each sample of the latent
field comes from a Gaussian distribution conditioned on the
just-sampled hyperparameters. Am I right? Or did I misunderstand
something?

Cheers,
Leo

--
Leonardo Bastos,
Public Health Ressearcher at Scientific Computing Program
Oswaldo Cruz Foundation, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
http://www.procc.fiocruz.br/Members/lsbastos/

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA posterior sample
parts:
Hi,

there isn't any paper on this (I just added it because we needed it at
some point).  the documentation says what happens

    The hyperparameters are sampled from the configurations used to do
     the numerical integration, hence if you want a higher resolution,
     you need to to change the ‘int.stratey’ variable and friends. The
     latent field is sampled from the Gaussian approximation
     conditioned on the hyperparameters, but with a correction for the
     mean (default).

although its to short to know really what is going on, maybe. 

as said, it uses the integration points to sample the hyperparameters,
so that is why you see only a finite number of configurations. for each
hyperparameter is sample the latent from the Gaussian approximation. In
most cases, ther is available a correction for the mean (like its
computed with the simplified.laplace or the laplace), then the mean of
this Gaussian is corrected, but the precision matrix is not. 

its possible to correct also for skewness, but no-one has got around to
do this as its potentially quite timeconsuming, well, maybe not. 

hope this helps!

PS: if someone wants to write this up properly and maybe do a
comparison, please let us know!

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA posterior sample
parts:
I am glad to see such feature as I may need it as well! 

Just to add one question about the latent field sampling. Letting the latent field be X={x_1, x_2,... x_k}, as far as I understand, INLA compute the marginal posterior distribution of the latent field, \pi(x_i|X_{-i},data), rather than the joint posterior \pi(X|data), right? If so, what about the sampling? Are the posterior samples generated using inla.posterior.samples from marginal posterior or joint posterior?

Thanks!
Michael

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA posterior sample
parts:
Hi,

while computing the posterior marginals, we also approximate the joint
with a Gaussian. the dependence comes from that one, while the
marginals are a little corrected for the mean. So, in technical terms,
we're using a Gaussian copula maintaining the marginals. (not strictly
true, as we can only do Gaussian marginals with are then mean
corrected, but in most cases, these samples are used to compute
something else and not marginals, so the error is smaller).

Best
H
